baseline.name: baseline-drew-rlm-head
baseline.note: Median of 3 deterministic runs. capHit identical across runs (deterministic path). After harness-fix at p.spec.layers, baseline still 0.452 — fix matters only for workspace-routed canonicals, not the baseline.

frontier.name: variant_b
frontier.note: Top on capHit and archetype yield. Swappable nodes pattern paid off — 3 canonical-emitter swaps during the run without disturbing flow wiring.

frontier.name: variant_a
frontier.note: Best latency via memoized brief lookup. Simplest code. Not Pareto-dominated — owns the latency frontier.

frontier.name: variant_c
frontier.note: Audit/replay infra is the win — zero on measured capHit delta, but 13 new tests incl. replay-purity proof + fold-only projections. Owns the observability frontier.

convergedFindings.axMiproV2Blocked: AxMiPRO v2 requires a Python optimizer sidecar (all three variants confirmed). AxBootstrapFewShot also fails via router+Haiku on all three. Fallbacks: corpus-mined rules (B), pure-demos artifact (A), instruction-only program (C).
convergedFindings.oracleCeiling: ~0.46-0.55 on ideasai given the hot-path planner's auto-attached framework/tailwind/shadcn/industry layers. The 3-layer expected sets in corpus/ideasai-prompts.json cannot be matched exactly while those auto-attaches are in place. Moving the ceiling requires either (a) modifying prompt-planner.ts (hot-path change, out of scope for this pursuit), or (b) changing the metric from strict Jaccard to 'expected ⊆ actual' precision-recall.
convergedFindings.harnessBug: scripts/meta-harness-eval.mjs:112 extractActual read p.layers instead of p.spec.layers for workspace plans — zeroed capability capture for any canonical prompt that expanded into a multi-lane plan. Fixed.

winner.reasoning: Top on the primary target metric (ideasaiCapHit) and on archetype yield. p95 of 0.986 ms is well under the 800 ms gate. AxFlow node contracts make the training/judge pipeline swappable, and the 3 canonical-emitter swaps during the run are the concrete proof.

nextGeneration.note: Current pursuit converged at the structural ceiling of the hot-path planner. To break 0.65 on ideasai, next generation must either change the planner's auto-attach behavior or change the capHit metric definition. Both are hot-path changes and require their own /pursue round.
nextGeneration.candidateMetricChange: Replace Jaccard with F1 or expected-as-subset-of-actual. Auto-attached layers are the user's DESIRED state (tailwind/shadcn are correct for any React SaaS) — penalizing them for not appearing in the hand-authored expected list is the metric's fault, not the planner's.
